candidate_074.name: predictive-failure-triggered M-open hypothesis expansion with confidence-gated contraction/reopening
candidate_074.mechanism_hypothesis: Maintain an evidence-weighted posterior over explicit mechanistic model structures instead of treating the current hypothesis set as closed. Score each freshly observed datum prequentially against the pre-observation best model, optionally combining it with robust backtests. If the target-space predictive residual exceeds a calibrated threshold, treat that as evidence that the current model support may be inadequate: ask a proposer for genuinely new structures conditioned on the residual patterns of the whole pool, then re-rank/prune them with Bayesian evidence and a complexity penalty. Conversely, when posterior mass concentrates and residuals are low, shrink an overgrown near-duplicate pool; if error rises or confidence falls again, reopen the pool. This creates an explicit control-state transition between search-support expansion and posterior concentration rather than merely spending more experiments inside a fixed model class.

primary_evidence.source: Kevin Murphy, Model Discovery Agent: LLM-assisted Bayesian experiment design for data-efficient discovery of mechanistic world models, arXiv:2608.09696v4, 2026-08-25.
primary_evidence.design: MDA combines an evidence-weighted SMC posterior over structured mechanistic models with information-driven experiment design. In the M-open extension, a predictive check evaluates the newly observed datum prequentially before the MAP model sees its outcome; the check can also backtest stored examples and uses a robust median error. When error exceeds a domain threshold, the LLM proposes a batch of new structures conditioned on residuals for the full current pool. CHEMBENCH evaluates a stratified 36-task subset (12 domains x easy/medium/hard) with two MDA seeds and held-out novel input conditions disjoint from the acquisition sequence.
primary_evidence.component_result: On CHEMBENCH, the paper reports overall mathematical-equivalence recovery of about 53% for full MDA versus about 42% for its rerun of LLM-AutoSciLab. Full MDA reaches about 62% on easy and 54% on medium tasks. On the hard compound-mechanism tier, full MDA and LLM-AutoSciLab are both about 42%, but removing M-open drops MDA to about 33%; the paper states the no-M-open ablation hurts every tier. The recovery curves plateau within roughly 10 experiments despite a budget of 60, so the remaining hard-tier gap is attributed to proposal-distribution coverage rather than simply more experiment rounds.
primary_evidence.support_control: The implementation treats hypothesis search as support control: births occur only when the predictive check fails, and top-posterior pruning is applied after expansion. The paper explicitly notes that correctness still assumes the LLM birth kernel eventually covers an adequate model; this is an assumption rather than a theorem.
primary_evidence.confidence_contraction: CHEMBENCH additionally starts with a model-pool cap of 16 and, once the MAP model is simultaneously high-confidence and low-residual, can shrink the cap to 6 to remove near-duplicate over-elaborated forms. The pool can re-expand when MAP error exceeds threshold or MAP confidence falls. The paper reports a small mathematical-equivalence improvement from this shrinkage but does not provide an isolated numeric effect size for the contraction rule.
primary_evidence.evaluation_boundary: The paper separates numerical fit from mechanism recovery: it gives examples where a baseline equation can achieve very low RMSLE while being mechanistically wrong, and therefore scores mathematical equivalence separately from held-out predictive error. This supports using predictive failure as a trigger without treating low prediction error alone as proof of mechanistic correctness.
primary_evidence.interpretation: This is a stronger open-world controller than candidate_073. Candidate_073 changes the acquisition objective between discriminating existing mechanisms and refining one surviving mechanism. candidate_074 changes the hypothesis support itself when predictive evidence says the current model class is inadequate, and later contracts/reopens that support as evidence changes. The direct causal evidence is strongest for the M-open expansion component; contraction/reopening has only a reported small improvement without a separately quantified ablation.
primary_evidence.limits: The strongest component evidence comes from simulator/oracle scientific benchmarks, not a live laboratory with sensor failures, batch effects, or costly physical interventions. M-open thresholds and pool settings are domain-specific; the contraction rule is demonstrated only on CHEMBENCH. The hard-tier result also exposes the central limitation: residual-triggered expansion cannot recover mechanisms the proposal distribution never generates. Nested SMC is compute-intensive, and this study does not isolate threshold sensitivity, prove autonomous threshold calibration, or combine model-class expansion with the separate measurement-fidelity and discovery-versus-generalization lane gates in candidates 072/071.

candidate_074.relation_to_existing: candidate_066 froze theory-discriminating experiments before execution; candidate_068 reserved theory-independent coverage against self-confirming adaptive sampling; candidate_071 separated discovery from generalization; candidate_072 added measurement admissibility; candidate_073 switched acquisition between mechanism discrimination and refinement based on confidence. candidate_074 addresses a different failure mode: the live hypothesis class itself can be wrong or incomplete, so predictive surprise should be able to expand model support and later contract/reopen it.
